question: At one digestion temperature, does a dose-response term improve prediction of cumulative methane at a dose the model has not seen?

eligibility.dose_unit: g_l (other bases only with a documented measured conversion)

split: whole-dose holdout: every replicate at the held-out dose is removed together
primary_metric: mean whole-dose-held-out RMSE (mL CH4 per g VS), each dose weighted equally

decision_rule.text: Select the simplest candidate unless a more complex candidate lowers the primary metric by more than 10% of the current candidate's value.

interpretation.constant_gompertz: No dose-response term is supported at this design.
interpretation.log_linear_dose_temperature: A monotone dose response is supported within the tested range.
interpretation.global_dose_temperature: A curved dose response is supported within the tested range.
interpretation.always: A within-study result. It is not held-out-study transfer, not evidence of mechanism, and says nothing beyond the tested dose range.

design_adequacy: Report the simulated recovery of the acquired dose grid (scripts/simulate_stage_a_power.py) next to the result. A grid without doses well beyond the expected optimum cannot reliably detect curvature.
secondary_reports: mean RMSE on interior doses only
prior_outcome_exposure: The Valentin & Białowiec (2024) parameter table and the Kozłowski (2025) trajectories were analysed before this specification was frozen. The rule was chosen from simulation only.
amendments: Any change requires a new specification id. Deviations after outcomes are seen must be labelled post hoc.
